question: Which of the following can be considered as an immediate cause of the Sanyasi Rebellion?

options.text: Implementation of the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act of 1908
Development of a broad sense of view of Indian Nationalism
British occupation of Madras region and their new land laws along with the atrocities of the landlords
Restrictions imposed by the British upon pilgrims visiting holy places among both Hindus and Muslims

solution:
The correct answer is option 4,Restrictions imposed by the British upon pilgrims visiting holy places among both Hindus and Muslims

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sanyasi Rebellion, which occurred during the late 18th century in Bengal, was primarily instigated by the **restrictions imposed by the British on religious pilgrimages**.
 
• Both Hindu and Muslim pilgrims faced severe obstacles as British policies curtailed their movement to holy places, violating their religious practices.
 
• These restrictions led to widespread resentment among the ascetics (Sanyasis) and Fakirs, who often traveled across regions for pilgrimage and sustenance.
 
• Additionally, the British imposed stringent economic conditions, such as high land taxes and exploitation by landlords, exacerbating the grievances of the common people.
 
• The rebellion was marked by armed resistance from both Sanyasis and Fakirs, showcasing their defiance against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanyasi Rebellion:**

 
 
• The Sanyasi Rebellion occurred primarily in Bengal and Bihar during the late 18th century.
 
• It involved Hindu ascetics (Sanyasis) and Muslim Fakirs who resisted British oppression.
 
• The rebellion was inspired by both religious and socio-economic grievances against colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Exploitation:**
 
 
• The British imposed high taxes and exploitative land revenue systems that severely impacted farmers and the rural economy.
 
• Landlords often worked in collaboration with the British, leading to atrocities against peasants.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Religious Practices:**
 
 
• The restrictions on pilgrimage were perceived as a direct attack on religious freedom by both Hindus and Muslims.
 
• This led to unification among religious groups against the British, creating a sense of collective resistance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Sanyasi Rebellion is considered one of the early resistances against British colonial rule in India.
 
• It highlighted the intersection of religious, economic, and social issues under colonial governance.
